answer.evidence: The seat width profile runs 6,8,10,10,8,6 over rows 17-22. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small purple-grey stool with a round seat and a pedestal base, about 7 distinct colours in total. It shows only about 3 lightness steps on the seat and column, against 5-6 on the references (the bench, the well, the stall). Its edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline does carry some tint. But the dark outline wraps the whole silhouette uniformly, which reads as a sticker-like line rather than selective dark material tones. There is little texture: no grain, speckle or per-part highlights, only a few highlight pixels on the seat. The per-tile tone counts are 0 because the piece is smaller than one tile, so I judged density by eye. It looks thinner and flatter than the bench, which has plank grain and highlights, and than the well, which has stones shaded one by one. A careful artist would not accept it beside the references.
